bindings.name: old_holder_commitment
bindings.source: envelope:holderBinding.commitment — a rebind is presented under the holder's current (old) identity, so this MUST equal the envelope holder binding.

bindings.name: new_holder_commitment
bindings.justification: The migration target is chosen by the holder: no request-side expected value exists for a freshly derived binding key. In-circuit it is derived from the new credential binding key via derive_holder_commitment and asserted distinct from the old commitment, and it is committed by claim_binding, so the verifier cannot be shown a swapped target. The verifier defensively re-checks new != old.

bindings.name: credential_id
bindings.justification: The verifier request vocabulary carries no credentialId expectation, and the rebind circuit carries no issuer signature, so this value is holder-asserted. It is swap-resistant because claim_binding commits to it together with the holder commitments and context. A consumer acting on the rebind (the issuer updating its binding record) MUST match this value against its own credential records before acting.

bindings.name: issuer_id_hash
bindings.justification: The rebind circuit carries no issuer signature, and the private credential_issuer_id_hash this public value is equated to is an unconstrained witness — the prover picks both sides of that equality, so absent a request pin this is a prover-chosen value with no attestation force. A consumer acting on the rebind MUST match it against its own records for the credential being rebound.
bindings.note: A request MAY pin the expected issuer via the issuerIdHash parameter; a supplied pin MUST be equality-checked and MUST be treated as a filter, never as attestation.

bindings.name: schema_id_hash
bindings.justification: The rebind circuit carries no issuer signature, and the private credential_schema_id_hash this public value is equated to is an unconstrained witness — the prover picks both sides of that equality, so absent a request pin this is a prover-chosen value with no attestation force. A consumer acting on the rebind MUST match it against its own records for the credential being rebound.
bindings.note: A request MAY pin the expected schema via the schemaIdHash parameter; a supplied pin MUST be equality-checked and MUST be treated as a filter, never as attestation.

bindings.name: proof_context
bindings.source: context:value — MUST equal the authenticated request context hash for this presentation.

bindings.name: timestamp
bindings.source: context:timestamp — MUST equal the authenticated request context timestamp.

bindings.name: claim_binding
bindings.note: compute_claim_binding_3 over the rebind public values; the verifier MUST recompute it so the public holders/credential/context cannot be swapped under a stale binding.
